title: U.S. House · Michigan's 2nd District
area: Michigan's 2nd Congressional District — the northwestern Lower Peninsula, including Midland and parts of the Grand Traverse region.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 2nd District R+15 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 64.3%–34.2% in 2024.
Incumbent John Moolenaar was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Ben Ambrose defeated Jamie Hill and Clyde Welford in the Democratic primary with 44.3% of the vote.

candidates.name: John Moolenaar
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Moolenaar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 2nd District, first elected in 2014. He previously served in the Michigan House and Michigan Senate and chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

background.text: Born in Midland, Michigan, in 1961; earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry from Hope College (1983) and a master's in public administration from Harvard University (1989).
Worked for Dow Chemical and later directed the Small Business Center for the Middle Michigan Development Corporation.
Served on the Midland City Council (1997–2000), in the Michigan House of Representatives (2003–2008), and in the Michigan Senate (2011–2015) before election to Congress.

priorities.text: Says he strongly supports the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative and will keep working across the aisle to secure funding for it.
priorities.quote: I strongly support the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI). Since the initiative was launched in 2010, GLRI funds have been used to support over 3,000 restoration projects to improve water quality, protect and restore native habitat, fight invasive species, and prevent beach closings.

priorities.text: Prioritizes building a replacement for the Soo Locks, describing an unscheduled closure as a threat to the North American industrial economy.
Says Congress must reduce federal spending and the national debt, and supports reforms to Social Security and Medicare that would not affect current retirees or those nearing retirement.

positions.summary: States that life begins at conception and that Congress should work to protect it, opposing legal abortion.
positions.quote: I believe that everyone has an unalienable right to life and that life begins at conception. We must work to protect life and ensure that every child has the opportunity to live life to the fullest.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a supporter of the Second Amendment and says the right to bear arms must be preserved.
positions.quote: As a supporter of the Second Amendment, I believe the right to bear arms is a fundamental principle upon which the founders built our nation. This right must be preserved for future generations.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Agriculture, Rural Development, FDA and Related Agencies; Labor, HHS, Education; National Security, Department of State and Related Programs subcommittees).

candidates.name: Ben Ambrose
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 44.3% of the vote

summary.text: Ambrose is a 20-year U.S. Marine Corps infantry veteran from Hesperia, Michigan, running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent John Moolenaar.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps for 20 years as an infantryman.
